a: A closure is a function that remembers variables from its outer scope even after that scope finished.
Hoisting moves declarations to the top of a scope; var/function behave differently than let/const.
The JS event loop processes the call stack and queues (microtasks/macrotasks) for async work.
JS objects inherit via the prototype chain.
this depends on how a function is called (object method, bind, arrow functions differ).
Arrow functions do not bind their own this; they use the enclosing scope's this.
obj?.prop safely accesses nested props without throwing if intermediate values are nullish.
a ?? b uses b only when a is null or undefined (not for 0 or '').
ES modules use import/export and are the standard module system in modern JS.
Event delegation listens on a parent and handles events from children via bubbling.
WeakMap keys are objects held weakly so they can be garbage-collected.
function* generators yield values lazily and can pause/resume execution.
Proxy intercepts object operations (get/set/has) for custom behavior.
